posts.caption:
Hiding your phone in another room isn't the fix. Turn its data off for your next hour.

iPhone: open Control Center and tap Wi-Fi and cellular data off.
Android: open Quick Settings and tap Internet (or Mobile data) and Wi-Fi off.
Turn them back on at 60 minutes. Calls and texts still get through.

Why: a direct retest of the famous phone-nearby study found no difference, but in a 2025 trial, blocking mobile internet for 2 weeks improved attention by about as much as 10 years of age-related decline. The trial ran 2 weeks; our 1-hour version borrows the idea.

Save this, send it to the friend with the phone-drawer rule and follow @lockedhourhq. The free 90-Day Lock-In Tracker is in our bio.

posts.caption:
Reach more of your goals: write one if-then plan tonight.

Pick a cue you can't miss: "When I sit down with coffee at 7:30..."
Name the first move: "...then I open the draft and type one line."
Plan for the obstacle: "If my phone buzzes, then I flip it face-down."

Why: across 94 independent tests, if-then plans had a medium-to-large effect on reaching goals (d = 0.65). It was the only one of 5 famous focus rules we checked that fully held up. Habits took 18 to 254 days in the classic study (not 21), and one missed day didn't derail them.

Save this, send it to the friend on day 22 of a 21-day challenge and follow @lockedhourhq. The free 90-Day Lock-In Tracker is in our bio.

posts.caption:
Start faster tomorrow: stop mid-sentence today.

At the end of your hour, leave the sentence, problem or slide half-done on purpose.
Write the next 3 words on a sticky note.
Tomorrow, finish that sentence first. No blank page.

Why: in a 2025 review of 21 studies, people went back to about 67% of interrupted tasks, well above the 50% chance rate. The lab gaps were 1 to 20 minutes; stopping overnight is our adaptation.

Save this, send it to someone with a thesis or big report and follow @lockedhourhq. The free 90-Day Lock-In Tracker is in our bio.

posts.caption:
Restart tomorrow, and start with one locked hour.

Name the fresh start: "Monday is Day 1."
Restart smaller: one hour, not a whole new routine.
Lock it with an if-then: "When I sit down after dinner Monday, then I start the timer."

Why: in a large data set of 11,912 students, the chance of a gym visit was 33% higher at the start of a week. The data is observational: it shows more starts on fresh starts, not that they last. That's why you keep it small.

Tomorrow is our fresh start too: the 90-Day Lock-In begins Monday. Save this, send it to your restart buddy and follow @lockedhourhq. The free tracker is in our bio.

posts.caption:
Lock one hour a day, every day, and you'll have 90 focused hours by Sat Jan 16. The 90-Day Lock-In starts today.

Pick your one task and write it on paper.
Write your if-then: "When I ___ at ___, then I start the timer."
Lock 60 minutes: data off, one task, timer on. Only 20 minutes today? It still counts.

Why 90 days and not 21: in studies, habits typically took about 2 months to form, and up to 254 days. Miss a day? In the classic habit study, one miss didn't derail it. Just never miss twice.

Joining? Comment IN, we reply by hand. Save this, send it to your accountability buddy and follow along. The free 90-Day Lock-In Tracker is in our bio.

posts.caption:
Get one focused hour tomorrow: follow this plan, minute by minute.

0:00 Say your if-then, turn Wi-Fi and data off, open one task.
0:45 Stop mid-sentence, write the next 3 words, then tomorrow's to-do list.
0:50 Walk with one question: walk for ideas, sit for answers.

Why: each move comes from research, from 94 tests of if-then plans to a 467-person trial that blocked phone data (for 2 weeks; we use 1 hour). The lab timings were different from ours, so treat the minutes as our version.

Save this, send it to the person you'd lock in with and follow @lockedhourhq. The free 90-Day Lock-In Tracker is in our bio.
